faq.q: What image formats and resolutions can I export?
faq.a: JPG, PNG or WEBP. DPI options are 72 (screen), 150 (recommended), 300 (print) and 600 (archival, large files). JPG and WEBP have a quality slider (20–100%); PNG is lossless so the slider is hidden. You can also set an exact output width/height in pixels with a "Fit within" or "Exact (may stretch)" mode, and an estimate shows the per-page dimensions and approximate file size before converting.

faq.q: Can I convert only some pages?
faq.a: Yes. All pages are shown as clickable thumbnails you can select individually, with All, None, Odd, Even and Invert buttons. A counter shows how many of the total are selected. Each selected page becomes its own image file, and you can save them one at a time, copy a page to the clipboard as PNG, or download everything as a ZIP.

faq.q: Are there image clean-up options for scans?
faq.a: Yes. Checkboxes let you crop white margins (auto-detects content bounds and trims with a small pad), convert to grayscale, and invert colours. Presets bundle sensible combinations: Web, Print, Archive, WhatsApp (low quality JPG), and Scan cleanup (300 DPI PNG with grayscale and margin crop on).

faq.q: Can I combine all pages into one image?
faq.a: Yes. "Stitch into one long image (PNG)" renders the selected pages and stacks them vertically into a single tall PNG, centred to the widest page — handy for sharing a whole document on WhatsApp as one image. Everything runs in your browser via pdf.js; files aren't uploaded, and your last format, DPI and quality are remembered locally under p2iFmt, p2iDpi and p2iQuality.
